customManagers.description: The pin of the previous-GA line.
The pin of the current-GA line, which is also the default of a plain build.
The pin of the preview line, which follows the alphas of the next minor.

packageRules.description: VanillaBP and the adapters follow the framework, not Renovate: their versions are bumped when a release is cut, and while they are snapshots there is nothing to look up.

The client pins are maintained by the custom managers above, one per line. Renovate's own maven manager sees the same dependency a second time through the dependencyManagement entry and would open a second pull request for a property one of those managers already owns.

Every line keeps its own pin, so a client update is proposed per line rather than as one shared PR: the lines are released separately and a failure on the preview must not hold up a bugfix on a GA line. A patch and a minor are separated here rather than repository-wide, because for these pins the two mean different things: upkeep inside the line, and a new line.
A patch of the client stays inside the line: the minimum cluster version does not move, so this is ordinary upkeep.

A minor of the client is a new line, not an update. The client a build was compiled against is the lowest cluster version that build accepts, so this bump raises the cluster requirement of everybody who consumes the line. It gets a branch of its own, waits for approval on the dependency dashboard and never merges itself. Rotating the lines is more than this pin: it also means a profile, the pin properties, the line table of the README and a release of the new line.
prBodyNotes: This crosses a release-line boundary. A Camunda 8 cluster and the applications running on it move together, and a cluster upgrade costs more organizationally than technically, which is why the lines exist at all. Merging this raises the lowest cluster version the built artifacts accept.
Before merging: is the new minor GA, does the line table of the README still describe reality, and does the previous GA line end with it?

packageRules.description: The preview line follows Camunda's alphas but not their release candidates: an -rc is a step on the way to an alpha, not something to build a published line on.
